name: Canberra Times cryptic crossword, Sunday 19 April 1992 (English cryptic)

clue.text: Having many attainments, left half to composer — and died!

indicators.note: half of a four-letter word keeps only two of its letters, here the front pair

blocks.note: the first half of the word left
Thomas Arne, the English composer of Rule, Britannia
D is the standard abbreviation for died

explanation.surface: A gifted person leaves half an estate to a composer and then dies.
explanation.walkthrough: LEARNED: half of left, then Arne, then D for died.
explanation.definitionFit: A learned person is erudite, having acquired much knowledge and many accomplishments through study.

clue.text: Listener's complaint

blocks.note: surface reading: a grumble from a radio listener
setter's reading: an ailment of the organ one listens with

explanation.walkthrough: A listener here is not a member of the radio audience but an ear, and the complaint is a medical one.
explanation.definitionFit: An earache is a pain in the ear, a complaint in the medical sense of an ailment.

clue.text: Scope for target practice?

blocks.note: first meaning: extent or reach
second meaning: a place laid out for shooting at targets

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second half is a definition by description, with 'for' meaning a place used for target practice.
explanation.definitionFit: A range is both the scope or extent of something and a ground where people practise shooting.

clue.text: Old flame-coloured matchhead in dug out

indicators.note: the match's tip is placed in the coloured word, sitting inside it

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner
hued means coloured
the head, or first letter, of match

explanation.surface: An old flame-coloured match head has been unearthed.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in flame-coloured hides the split between Old flame and coloured, and matchhead means only the head of the match.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhume is to dig up something buried, especially a body from a grave.

clue.text: Hooted at performance after free admission

indicators.note: a performance that has admitted something now holds it inside, so the word for free goes within

blocks.note: a deed is an act or performance
to rid is to free of something

explanation.surface: An audience let in without paying jeers the show anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: Free admission reads as a ticket, but it means the performance admits the word for free.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoot at someone is to mock them with jeering noises, which is what deriding means.

clue.text: Amorous book-bearing schoolboy

indicators.note: a schoolboy bearing something carries it, holding it within

blocks.note: Eric, hero of the Victorian school story Eric, or Little by Little
OT, the Old Testament, a book of the Bible

explanation.surface: A lovesick schoolboy carries his books around.
explanation.walkthrough: Eric is the crossword's stock schoolboy, from Dean Farrar's 1858 novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Erotic means arousing or concerned with sexual desire, close to amorous.

clue.text: In other words — 'tisn't free!

indicators.note: put into other words, the phrase is recast with its letters in a new order

blocks.note: the letters of tisn't free

explanation.surface: Put plainly, it is not free of charge.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a price; the letters of tisn't free, put into other words, give IN FETTERS, which itself means not free.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in fetters is shackled in chains, so is not at liberty.

clue.text: Escape! (Monkey leaves, starting east in headgear that's forfeiture)

indicators.note: the animal leaves the word, so its letters are taken out
the letter is put in the headgear, sitting inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
an ape is a monkey in loose usage
a hat is headgear
the first letter of east

explanation.surface: A monkey escapes, setting off east in a hat it may lose.
explanation.walkthrough: Escape! looks like the definition, but it is raw material; forfeiture at the far end defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Escheat is the old legal reversion of property to the Crown or lord when its holder dies without heirs, a kind of forfeiture.

clue.text: The sort of justice that makes Martine fatter

indicators.note: the name and the adjective are made into something new, their letters reworked

blocks.note: the letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A kind of rough justice that leaves a woman called Martine heavier.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair treatment is even-handed dealing, which is what justice delivers.

clue.text: Interior of farm building modified for husks

indicators.note: something modified has been altered, so the inner letters are rearranged

blocks.note: a barn is a farm building; only its interior, the middle pair, is changed

explanation.surface: Changes inside a barn are made to store husks.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the inside of the building's name is changed; its first and last letters stay put.
explanation.definitionFit: Bran is the husk of cereal grain separated from the flour during milling.

clue.text: Main administrative centre to deflect diamonds

blocks.note: to head off is to divert or turn aside
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A central bureau tries to stop diamonds being diverted.
explanation.definitionFit: A head office is the principal headquarters from which an organisation is run.

clue.text: Outcry caused by well known runner crossing centre of arena

indicators.note: the centre of a five-letter word is its third letter alone
a runner crossing something straddles it, so that letter sits within

blocks.note: scram! is the familiar order to run off, the setter's runner
the middle letter of arena

explanation.surface: A famous athlete crossing the stadium causes a public outcry.
explanation.walkthrough: E goes inside SCRAM to give SCREAM. The athlete Steve Cram fits the surface but would leave the S unexplained, so the runner is the word scram.
explanation.definitionFit: A scream is a loud cry, and an outcry is a loud shout or clamour.

clue.text: Member of mimosa family puts king on course

blocks.note: R for rex, Latin for king
Aintree is the racecourse near Liverpool where the Grand National is run

explanation.surface: A monarch plants an acacia-like shrub on a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: The rain tree is a large tropical tree of the legume subfamily once called the mimosa family.

clue.text: Extremely likeable wild garden — seen at end of May, it's fabulous!

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of a word, its outermost letters
a wild garden is untamed and disordered, so its letters run riot
the end of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: the first and last letters of likeable
garden rearranged
the last letter of May

explanation.surface: A charming overgrown garden at the end of May is a fairy-tale sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fabulous is the stuff of fable, and legendary describes what belongs to legend.

clue.text: Incorporating substance into oriental pottery

indicators.note: one thing put into another sits inside it

blocks.note: E for eastern
Ming porcelain, from China's Ming dynasty
body is substance, as in a wine with body

explanation.surface: A material is being mixed into a piece of Eastern pottery.
explanation.walkthrough: Oriental pottery reads as one phrase, but oriental gives only E and the substance goes into the pottery alone.
explanation.definitionFit: To embody is to include or contain something as part of a whole, which is incorporating.

clue.text: Trifling protest initiated against British painter

indicators.note: something initiated has only just begun, so only the word's opening letter counts

blocks.note: the first letter of protest
William Etty, the Victorian painter of nudes

explanation.surface: A minor objection is raised against a British artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Petty means small and unimportant, which is what trifling describes.

clue.text: House builder's party in Lincoln

indicators.note: a party held in a person sits inside that name

blocks.note: Abe, the familiar name of Abraham Lincoln
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A builder throws a party at President Lincoln's house.
explanation.walkthrough: DO goes inside ABE, after its A. The 's stands for is.
explanation.definitionFit: Adobe is sun-dried mud brick, the material houses are built from in dry countries.

clue.text: Everybody starts to hang about part of the pool

indicators.note: a word's start is its first letter only
to hang about something is to surround it, so that letter goes inside

blocks.note: to depend is, in an old sense, to hang down from
the first letter of everybody

explanation.surface: Everyone begins to loiter by part of the swimming pool.
explanation.walkthrough: E goes inside DEPEND. Depend's literal sense is to hang down, as in a chandelier depending from a ceiling.
explanation.definitionFit: The deep end is the section of a swimming pool where the water is deepest.

clue.text: Kind missile may be left one second in sea

indicators.note: letters placed in a sea sit inside that sea's name

blocks.note: the Baltic Sea of northern Europe
L for left
the Roman numeral for one
S for second

explanation.surface: A warning that some type of missile might be left in the sea for a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: Kind missile may be is a definition by example: the answer is a kind a missile may be.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballistic missile is a kind of missile that follows a free-falling arc after its powered launch.

clue.text: Muriel's redrafted article on hypothetical land

indicators.note: a redrafted text is rewritten, so the name's letters take a new order

blocks.note: the name, with 's meaning is
a, the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Muriel has rewritten her article about a theoretical country.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemuria was a lost continent proposed in the 1800s to explain the spread of lemurs across the Indian Ocean.

clue.text: Fit as a fashionable fe male installing a piano

indicators.note: the female installing something houses it within

blocks.note: in means fashionable
she, a female
taken as written
p, the musical mark for soft (piano)

explanation.surface: A trendy woman putting in a piano is clearly in good condition.
explanation.walkthrough: The newspaper's typesetting splits female across a line break; read it as one word. Piano is the musical direction for soft.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in shape is to be physically fit and in good condition.

clue.text: Artist beginning to look round container, being short of pigment

indicators.note: a beginning is a word's first letter, used for both words that follow

blocks.note: the first letter of artist
the first letter of look
a bin is a container
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A painter starts to inspect a pot, finding it lacks colour.
explanation.definitionFit: An albino is a person or animal born lacking the pigment melanin, so is pale.

clue.text: The unplumed variety that goes from side to side

definitions.text: that goes from side to side

indicators.note: a variety is a different form, so the letters take on another arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A featherless bird species waddles from side to side.
explanation.definitionFit: A pendulum is a weight hung from a fixed point that swings back and forth.

clue.text: Simple style associated with holy man

blocks.note: a mode is a style or fashion
ST, abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A plain way of dressing is linked with a saint.
explanation.definitionFit: Modest and simple both describe something unpretentious and without show.

clue.text: Possible treatment for eye doctor works

blocks.note: DR, abbreviation for doctor
ops, plural of op, short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: An eye doctor's operations as a possible treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: Eye doctor looks like one phrase, but eye belongs to the definition and doctor starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Eye drops are liquid medicine dripped into the eye, a common treatment.

clue.text: One requesting small charge goes before Queen

blocks.note: petit is French for small
an ion is an electrically charged particle
ER, for Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A person asking the monarch to waive a small fee appears before her.
explanation.definitionFit: A petitioner is someone who makes a formal request or appeal.

clue.text: Stone work finished off with aluminium

blocks.note: op. is the abbreviation for opus, a work
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: Masonry is given a metal finish.
explanation.walkthrough: Stone work reads as masonry, but Stone alone defines and work starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An opal is a gemstone, prized for its shifting play of colours.

clue.text: Grand entry in Aida production — with big slow movements

indicators.note: an entry into something goes inside it
a new production of an opera restages it, so its letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand
Verdi's opera
OS for outsize

explanation.surface: A grand entrance in a staging of Verdi's opera involves large, slow processions.
explanation.definitionFit: An adagio is a piece or movement of music played at a slow tempo.

clue.text: Ghost of female in grip of poison

indicators.note: whatever is held in something's grip is enclosed by it

blocks.note: bane is an old word for poison, as in henbane
she, the female pronoun

explanation.surface: A woman's ghost appears in the grip of a poison.
explanation.definitionFit: A banshee is a wailing female spirit of Irish folklore whose cry foretells a death.
